Subject: Dedicated capacity — throughput acceptance & measurement plan

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for the time last week. As we start to formalize the committed GPU pool and discount bands, you asked for a concrete, testable acceptance methodology for the throughput and latency guarantees. I pulled together a short proposal below so we have a single source of truth to review with your procurement and SRE teams.

Summary (ask):
- Redwood proposes a 30-day committed capacity window (reserved pool) with a tokens/sec guarantee measured at the pool level.
- Acceptance test: 60-minute sustained run with specified request mix and KV-cache warm/cold phases (details below).
- Pass criteria: Sustained 90th-percentile tokens/sec within 10% of the committed tokens/sec target AND 95th-percentile tail latency below agreed threshold.

Why this matters: we want a reproducible, production-like test that accounts for request concurrency, prompt length distribution, and cache effects so your app sees the same economics in production as in the contract.

Proposed next steps:
1) Review the attached draft playbook (short) on measurement harness and seed prompts.
2) Agree on the committed tokens/sec, latency SLOs, and acceptable burst window.
3) Schedule a 60-minute verification run in your staging region (we can run jointly).

Open questions for you:
- Do you prefer guarantees expressed as tokens/sec (pool-level) or requests/sec per instance?
- Any constraints on time windows for acceptance tests (e.g., must be during business hours)?

I'll loop in Karthik for the technical runbook items and Laura for contractual acceptance/credits.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — throughput acceptance & measurement plan

Hi Sam —

Below is a concise, operational measurement plan you can share with SRE. I've attached the raw run CSV from our lab run on 2027-03-10 for reference. Quick highlights:

1) Metrics we measure (definitions):
- tokens/sec (pool-level): total output tokens produced by the pool divided by wall-clock seconds over the test window (sustained measurement).
- requests/sec (RPS): number of requests accepted by the pool per second (useful for mapping to per-tenant TPS).
- latency p95/p99: end-to-end model emission latency measured from request arrival to final token. We record both emission-only and end-to-end.

2) Test composition (60-minute official run):
- Phase A (first 10 minutes): cold cache baseline — fresh model and KV cache cold-start; 30% of requests use long prompts (avg 512 tokens), 70% short (avg 64 tokens).
- Phase B (40 minutes): steady-state warmed KV caches; request mix modeled from your traffic sample (we propose: 50% short/30% medium/20% long; see attached seed prompts).
- Phase C (last 10 minutes): burst window — allow up to 25% above committed tokens/sec for 5 minutes to confirm graceful degradation and no hard failures.

3) Acceptance criteria (pass):
- Sustained pool-level tokens/sec averaged over the steady-state phase (Phase B) >= 90% of committed tokens/sec target.
- 95th-percentile end-to-end latency during Phase B <= agreed latency target (for example: 300 ms for short prompts, 800 ms for long prompts).
- No request error rate > 0.5% during the test.

4) Mapping tokens/sec -> per-tenant expectations:
- We deliver pool-level guarantees. Allocation to tenants can be done by reservation policies (static per-tenant caps) or token-based throttles in your gateway. We can provide a mapping table showing expected RPS for common prompt length quantiles to help you size per-tenant caps.

5) Measurement tooling & reproducibility:
- We recommend using the Redwood test harness (redbench) with deterministic seeds; all logs and raw token timestamps are exported.
- We will jointly run the harness from your staging VPC to include network behavior.

6) Credits & remediation (proposal):
- If acceptance run fails to meet pass criteria, Redwood will offer a one-time credit equal to 10% of one month’s committed fee OR allow a re-run after remediation work within 7 days. For repeated failures post-onboarding, sliding credits escalate per contract.

Attachments: dedicated-benchmark-run-20270310.csv (sample run), redwood-throughput-playbook-v1.pdf

Happy to walk this through in a 30-min call and adjust thresholds to match your UX targets.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sam —

Thanks Karthik — that playbook is the level of detail procurement needs. A few contract-level clarifications we typically include in the SOW and we can tailor them: 
- Acceptance window: the test will be scheduled within 14 days after contract signing. Both parties will nominate an SRE/ops lead to coordinate the run.
- Measurement authority: measurement results will be jointly validated; logs and raw CSVs will be exchanged and stored in the Drive link below.
- Credits: proposed credit = 10% one-time credit OR free remedial engineering + re-run. We can make credits tiered if you prefer (e.g., 5%-15% depending on severity / duration shortfall).
- Discount bands: to hit the committed rate of X tokens/sec you will be quoted Y% discount. If you choose a higher commit band (tier), discount increases but acceptance targets scale accordingly.

I'll draft sample SOW language this afternoon and post it to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redwood-playbook.
